subject: Renewal pricing: VPC surcharge + capacity uplift reconciliation
messages:
From: Cara Nguyen <cara.nguyen@orchid-retail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@orchid-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal — VPC surcharge and capacity uplift reconciliation

Hi Soojin,

We received the renewal outline from your team and have two items blocking approval from procurement: the VPC/private deployment surcharge in the dedicated pricing, and the proposed capacity uplift SKU (the next-tier commit). Before we route to legal and finance, procurement has asked for a clear reconciliation showing: 1) effective unit price at current run-rate vs proposed commit, 2) one-time credits or concessions tied to the uplift, and 3) how long any price hold would last once we commit.

We can flex on term length, but need a breakdown that shows net TCO for the first 12 months (including VPC egress/managed-network fees). We’ve attached our internal usage report (Q4) for reference — note: we expect a 30% uplift in peak inference volume if we onboard a new personalization pipeline in Q3.

Can you put together the reconciliation and a recommended path (e.g., stepped commit, temporary credits) by EOD next Thursday?

Thanks,
Cara
Cara Nguyen
VP, Cloud Engineering
Orchid Retail

Attachments: usage_report_q4.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Cara Nguyen <cara.nguyen@orchid-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — VPC surcharge and capacity uplift reconciliation

Hi Cara — thanks for the clear ask and the usage file. I’m proposing two practical options so procurement and finance have choice depending on risk appetite:

Option A — Staggered commit (recommended):
- 6-month pilot commit = 60% of requested uplift at 12% discount off list for dedicated GPU pool.
- Auto-accelerator: if run-rate > 85% of pilot commit for two consecutive months, full uplift triggers and pricing reverts to 15% discount on that volume.
- One-time onboarding credit: $50,000 applied to first invoice.
- VPC surcharge: waive managed-network surcharge for first 3 months; thereafter apply standard surcharge line item.

Option B — Full year commit + price hold:
- 12-month committed uplift at 15% discount;
- Price hold guarantee for 90 days after signing (protects against mid-quarter rate moves);
- Reduced one-time credit: $30,000. VPC surcharge waived for first month only.

I’ve attached a quick SKU worksheet and a VPC pricing breakdown that maps the surcharge line items; the net effective unit costs are shown in tab 'net_tco'. If you prefer, we can structure a hybrid (6-month pilot with a conditional credit tranche that triggers on go-live).

Next steps: if either option looks sensible, I’ll share an addendum (v3) and loop in legal for a narrow amendment. Ben — want to weigh in on concessions/credit sizing?

Best,

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0132
A: 220 Market St, San Francisco, CA

Attachments: vpc_pricing_breakdown.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB), orchid_redwood_renewal_SKU_notes.xlsx (XLSX, 38KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — VPC surcharge and capacity uplift reconciliation

Thanks Soojin — reviewed both options. Approve moving forward with Option A as our customer-friendly default. Approvals:

- One-time onboarding credit: authorize $50,000 (to be recorded as contra-revenue),
- Pilot discount cadence: approve 12% pilot discount with automatic step-up to 15% on sustained usage trigger,
- VPC surcharge concession: waive managed-network surcharge for first 6 weeks (slightly more than proposed) — this is an operational concession tied to onboarding support, not a permanent price change,
- Price hold: internal price-hold approval limited to 90 days post-signing.

Note: require a brief addendum that codifies the trigger (85% run-rate for two months) and the schedule for the one-time credit. Marissa — please attach the required revenue accounting note and confirm the contra-revenue tagging before we issue the addendum.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Internal: financial impact estimated at ~$120k P&L hit in Q2 if fully utilized; acceptable for strategic retention.
